visuals.caption: Matched news retrieval on 172 previously examined MultiHop-RAG questions. Counts are sealed normalised exact matches, not evidence coverage. All arms use labelled two-sentence windows, cosine plus 0.5 normalised BM25, deterministic article-ordered delivery within 2000 cl100k tokens, and the same Claude Sonnet 5.5 low-effort reader with answer-form rules. Facet-conditioned retrieval ranks within exact outlet/date supports and merges facets round-robin. RAG uses a 200-candidate pool with MMR relevance coefficient 0.7. RAPTOR searches 1747 summary nodes plus the same labelled windows without MMR. The rules were developed after examining failures on all 172 questions. These descriptive reused-draw counts show a tie between facet-conditioned retrieval and RAG, with RAPTOR four answers lower, not established superiority or equivalence.

visuals.title: FRAMES: distinguish the endpoint
visuals.reader_purpose: Show that answer-form matching and rubric correctness answer different questions under the same recommended no-activation route.
visuals.entry: Reader understands missing-needs retrieval and fixed allowances, but may confuse page presence, containment and correctness.
visuals.exit: Reader can read123/117 proxy and127/126 judged counts separately, and interpret seven–six judged discordances without importing activation page statistics.

controls.budget: 8k initial + up to 4k genuinely new spans on one triggered pass 2
controls.settings: FRAMES pass-1 RAG uses a 200-candidate pool and MMR with relevance coefficient 0.7, ranked from s + 0.4 h/max(h), where s = cosine + 0.2 normalised BM25 and h is D's dense seed. Pass 2 ranks each missing-need phrase by s(phrase)+0.5 s(question), using RAG's own MMR 0.7. Both arms receive the same 8k initial allowance, steps instruction and up to 4k new spans on one triggered second pass. These are the local implemented comparator settings, not a claim of complete literature-system reproduction.

endpoint.definition: the implemented normalised first-clause/token-F1>=0.5 proxy with a3x length guard, not a semantic entailment certificate.
endpoint.qualification: Implemented normalised first-clause/token-F1 >=0.5 proxy with3x length guard. Not exact string containment, semantic entailment, judged correctness or all-gold-page coverage.

visuals.caption: FRAMES outcomes on the same 190 previously examined questions, with activation switched off for linked-passage retrieval. Both arms receive 8000 initial tokens, the same steps instruction and at most one triggered retrieval of 4000 genuinely new tokens for reader-declared missing needs. Linked-passage retrieval uses a 50-piece head and a one-hop link witness with merged-section delivery. RAG uses MMR relevance coefficient 0.7 over a 200-candidate pool. Its separate 0.4 coefficient weights the dense seed, not MMR. Pass-2 missing-need ranking combines the phrase score with 0.5 times the question score. The containment proxy is normalised substring/first-clause matching or token-F1 at least 0.5, subject to a three-times-reference length guard, with exact matches also counted. Judged correctness uses the banked majority rubric, not that proxy. The judged discordances are seven linked-passage-only successes and six RAG-only successes. The observed one-answer difference is modest, not evidence of general superiority. Page presence alone need not deliver an answer-bearing passage, particularly where the plaintext corpus omits tables.

visuals.caption: Source location and claim support in the Wyoming climate example. The stored witness is the first sentence of a three-sentence source unit. It supports the southeastern-vulnerability statement. The westward decline and small, brief tornado statements require the following source context, reproduced here. The five-field record is a model-produced assertion, not an entailment certificate. Its returned unit identifier contains a recorded typo and was assigned by position to the requested source unit. The original request, response and processed span identities remain in the supporting record. A located quote establishes provenance for that span, not support for every field.

visuals.methods: Shared improved index and dated turn keys, completed rules reading, no ledger, same Sonnet low reader.
visuals.endpoint: 48 includes6abstentions;42 excludes all6; historical44 includes2annotated abstentions and is not plotted.
visuals.caption: Completed LongMem readout on a shared improved index at 4000- and 8000-token allowances, using Claude Sonnet 5.5 at low effort and the same rules instruction. Correctness includes all 48 questions, including six abstention questions. Complete positive-evidence coverage counts questions for which every annotated required turn is delivered, restricted to the 42 positive-evidence questions. This is turn-ID coverage, not semantic entailment or answer correctness. Relational and dense retrieval coincide on both endpoints in this shared-index setting. Hybrid retrieval improves from 40 to 44 correct answers and from 33 to 37 positive questions with all required turns as the allowance increases. The distinct historical 44-annotation endpoint includes two annotated abstentions and is retained separately in the audit, not relabelled as positive coverage.
